vacuous_test_check.method: Considered whether a stub run_clean_clone (e.g. always returning success without actually cloning or running tests) would pass. test_fails_closed_when_test_dirties_clone specifically writes a real file from within a real subprocess-executed test and asserts the runner detects the resulting dirty working tree via a real `git status` call; a stub would not perform any real git operations and would fail this test's setup expectations (no actual clone would exist to check).
vacuous_test_check.result: NOT_VACUOUS -- and confirmed doubly non-vacuous by my own real-repository hidden case, which exercises the entire pipeline (real git clone, real detached checkout, real git ls-tree discovery, real subprocess test execution, real git status dirty-check) against production data neither the producer's fixtures nor I had staged in advance.

additional_findings.disclosed_limitation_assessment: The disclosed limitation (remote clone transport not tested) is honest and appropriately scoped -- the required_deliverable only asks for cloning 'into a caller-supplied directory' from a 'repository', which is satisfied by local-path cloning; nothing in the acceptance criteria mandates remote/network transport testing, and the forbidden list explicitly disallows treating network dependencies as acceptable, so local-only transport is the correct and safer choice.
